prompt: One of the exact-value angles: $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{n}$. What is $n$?
hint: $\sin 30^\circ$ is the HEIGHT of the point at $30^\circ$ on the unit circle. It is exactly half of the radius.

hints.text: $\sin 30^\circ$ is the HEIGHT of the point at $30^\circ$ on the unit circle. It is exactly half of the radius.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $\sin 90^\circ$: the point is $(0, 1)$, so the height is $1$. Now ask the same question at $30^\circ$ — is that height bigger or smaller than $1$? It turns out to be exactly half.

explanation: The point at $30^\circ$ on the unit circle is $\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$.
Sine reads the height, which is $\frac{1}{2}$ — exactly half the radius.

alternativeExplanations.title: The half-equilateral triangle
steps: Draw an equilateral triangle with sides of length 1. Every angle is 60°.
Slice it down the middle. The half is a right triangle with a 30° angle, a long side of 1, and a short side of exactly 1/2 — because the slice cut a side of length 1 in half.
That short side is the height at 30°, so sin 30° = 1/2.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sanity-check the size
steps: Sine is a height on a circle of radius 1, so it always sits between 0 and 1 in the top half.
30° is only a third of the way to the top (90°), so the height should be small. 1/2 = 0.5 fits; 1/3 or 1/4 would be too low for 30°.
